Student Score Analysis
Level 1 — Remembering

scores = [78, 92, 85, 67, 88, 95, 73]
Functions: find_highest(scores), find_lowest(scores), calculate_average(scores), main()
Return the highest score, lowest score, and average. Do not use max(), min(), or sum(). main() creates the list, calls each function, and prints:
Highest score: 95
Lowest score: 67
Average score: 82.57
responses.explanation:
the goal of the code is to find max min and average value of the given list. Line 1 initializes the list, line 2 creates main function that calls the rest of the functions and prints them out. Line 9 to 13 defines find high function that iterates though the entire list (line 10) and updates high variable value at every comparision (line 11-12)
The same applies for find lowest  (line 16 for iterating through the list, comparing at 17-18) and average ( line 22 for iterating and updating average value at 23-24)

responses.question:
Course Enrollment Dictionary
Level 2 — Understanding

course_enrollment = {"CSCI 110": 32, "CSCI 204": 28, "CSCI 311": 24, "MATH 201": 35}
Functions: add_course(course_enrollment, course_code, enrollment), update_enrollment(course_enrollment, course_code, enrollment), find_course(course_enrollment, course_code), display_courses(course_enrollment), main()
add_course() and update_enrollment() return True on success, False otherwise. find_course() returns the enrollment or None. Display format: CSCI 204: 30 students
In main(), perform in order — add "CSCI 320" (20); attempt to add "CSCI 204" (40); update "CSCI 204" to 30; attempt to update "PHYS 211" to 25; search "CSCI 311" and "PHYS 211"; display all records. Print a clear message showing whether each operation succeeded.
responses.explanation:
Chain of thoughts:
we will have the functions outlined as above  where add course function should point to the end of the dictionary and insert a new element specifying its key and value fields.The update enrollment should iterate through dictionary elements and find the course using the key of the dictionary. If it matches it should print out the specific dictionary element that matches the search inquiry

responses.question:
Document Processing Stack
Level 3 — Applying
A department processes documents most-recent-first.

actions = [("push", "Research Proposal"), ("push", "Travel Request"),
           ("push", "Purchase Request"), ("peek",), ("pop",),
           ("push", "Course Revision Form"), ("size",),
           ("pop",), ("pop",), ("pop",), ("pop",)]
Functions: push(stack, document), pop(stack), peek(stack), is_empty(stack), stack_size(stack), display_stack(stack), main()
Use a Python list with its end as the top. push() returns the new size. pop() returns the top document or None if empty. peek() returns the top without removing it, or None. display_stack() prints top to bottom without modifying the stack. main() processes each action, printing the result and the stack after each — e.g. Added to stack: Purchase Request, The stack is empty. No document was removed.
responses.explanation: The purpose of this code is to utilize stack system to keep track of department documents where pop and push functions are used ot retreieve latest element(LIFO), and  update the elements within our stack

responses.question:
Academic Advising Queue
Level 4 — Analyzing
Students see an adviser in arrival order; some leave first.

actions = [("arrive", "Aisha"), ("arrive", "Benjamin"), ("arrive", "Carlos"),
           ("arrive", "Diana"), ("leave", "Carlos"), ("arrive", "Emily")]
Functions: add_student(waiting_queue, student_name), assist_next_student(waiting_queue), remove_student(waiting_queue, student_name), display_queue(waiting_queue), main()
Use a Python list. add_student() appends to the back. assist_next_student() removes and returns the front, or None if empty. remove_student() removes a named student and returns True, or False if not found — remaining students keep their order. main() processes all actions, displaying the queue after each and at the end — e.g. Aisha joined the queue., Carlos left the queue.
In a comment above each function, state and justify its time complexity.
responses.explanation: The task asks to create a queue system for which we can utilize queue class and assign front and back pointers to

responses.question:
Sorting and Searching Course Scores
Level 5 — Evaluating

course_scores = [78, 92, 85, 67, 88, 95, 73, 81, 90, 76]
search_scores = [85, 90, 100]
Functions: linear_search_score(course_scores, target_score), binary_search_score(sorted_scores, target_score), display_scores(course_scores), main()
Both searches return the index when found, -1 otherwise. Linear searches the original list; binary searches a sorted copy (sorted() is allowed here). main() displays the original list, linear-searches every value in search_scores, displays the sorted list, then binary-searches the same values.
Original Scores:
78 92 85 67 88 95 73 81 90 76
Score 85 found at index 5.
Score 100 was not found.
responses.explanation: goal is to find the scores in the list using both linear and binary search where binary search utilizes pre sorted list (line 12). Time complexity for linear search is O(n) and for binary search its O.

responses.question:
Grocery List Manager
Level 6 — Creating

groceries = [("Milk", 2), ("Bread", 1), ("Eggs", 12),
             ("Rice", 1), ("Apples", 6), ("Chicken", 2)]
shopping_requests = ["Eggs", "Milk", "Chocolate", "Rice", "Bananas", "Bread"]
Functions: create_grocery_table(groceries), add_item(grocery_table, item_name, quantity), remove_item(grocery_table, item_name), display_grocery_list(grocery_table), main()
Convert the list into a dictionary {item_name: quantity}. Add "Cheese" (1); attempt to add "Milk" again; remove "Rice"; attempt to remove "Coffee" — print a message for each. Then queue all requests in a list and process them FIFO, printing whether each was found and its quantity. Finally display the table alphabetically without sort() or sorted().
Cheese was added.        Item found: Eggs, Quantity: 12
Milk already exists.     Chocolate was not found.
responses.explanation: the goal of the code is to create grocery shopping functions  that helps to add convert the grocery item list into dictionaries with the quantity of the items and their names. Additionally we need to  create supplemental functions that will help to update dictionary values to keep quantities updates and add_item funciton to add new dictionary elements to the lest. Display function should follow FIFO rule where  the first element of the list will be output first and continue in the same pattern until all of the list elements are displayed
